note: Franky's notebook. Written by the duck itself (the model's weights never change). tries = attempts the note was shown in, wins = how many of those succeeded.

knowledge.text: Moving forward 0.3m can cause the green box to become invisible in the camera view.
The beak successfully picks up the banana if its long side is within 87 degrees of lying across my beak.
Safety system refuses walks if the box rim would trip me (e.g., Step 5, 6).
Opening the beak near the box drops the banana on the table, not inside it.
Turning 90 degrees right results in a slight overshoot (e.g., 92 degrees turn, 0.03 m forward).
Asking for 180 degrees left results in a 180 degree turn to the right.
Asking for 0 degrees turn and 0.3m forward results in a 7 degree left turn and 0.29m forward movement.

skills.text: If the target is lost after moving, turn around 180 degrees to try and find it again.
Use measure() to confirm the exact distance and bearing of the target before attempting to drop the banana.
Since I cannot walk into the box, I must find a way to manipulate the banana after dropping it.
If the target is not found, try moving forward small amounts (e.g., 0.1m) and turning slightly (e.g., 5 degrees) to explore the area.
Turning 180 degrees is not guaranteed to re-establish visual contact with the target.
